ownership_reason: Only the gold walks the tree from a node that records no source file name and decides at which node the walk stops; hop 1 answers a null node, hop 2 a node with a name of its own, and hops 3-4 hand a nameless node on. The facade's contract is 'the source name property on the node or its ancestors': a nameless node belongs to the file recorded on its nearest ancestor that records one, whatever that ancestor's kind. On the trigger tree (a BLOCK below a BLOCK that records "foo", no SCRIPT) the gold walks past the recording ancestor and returns null for every node it can be given, so no caller that keeps the gold's output can recover the name without walking the tree again itself. The convention that a record on a node that is not a SCRIPT names the file of the nodes below it is pinned outside the gold: NodeTraversal.traverseAtScope and SyntacticScopeCreator.scanRoot take the source name for a whole function scope from the FUNCTION root's own record; Node.copyInformationFrom and IRFactory.createTemplateNode put the record on ordinary nodes (every parsed node, every node made from another), not only on SCRIPTs; CreateSyntheticBlocksTest.testUnmatchedStartMarker reports a warning whose source name comes from a CALL node's own record through NodeUtil.getSourceName and CompilerTestCase requires that name; GlobalVarReferenceMapTest and AstValidatorTest pin that a SCRIPT's own record counts. The gold's javadoc promises the name of the source file that the node belongs to; the trigger's node hangs below an ancestor that records "foo".
